newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY CONFIRMS MINISTER'S RESIGNATION OFFER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY CONFIRMS MINISTER'S RESIGNATION OFFER.

text.p: The Hungarian Prime Minister's Office on Thursday confirmed that welfare minister Gyorgy Szabo has offered his resignation but said Prime Minister Gyula Horn has not yet accepted it.
"(Horn) has received the offer of resignation but no decision has yet been made," Horn's press spokeswoman Eszter Puchmann told Reuters.

Szabo would be the ninth minister to resign from Horn's coalition government of Socialists and Free Democrats since it was formed in May 1994. All but one have been appointees of Horn's Socialist Party.

Recent weeks have also seen the removal by Horn of the entire board of the State Privatisation Agency APV over irregular pyments to a consultant and the resignation of two vice-presidents of the National Bank over an unfavourable options deal which cost the bank billions of forints.

Szabo is reported to have offered his resignation for personal reasons. His department is coming under strong pressure to cut its spending as the social security deficit has widened this year to three times the 1996 target of 17.8 billion forints.
On Tuesday the president of the Hungarian Hospitals Federation warned that unless hospitals' debts are settled immediately 49 hospitals across Hungary will run out of blood plasma and medicines.
